title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In this fourth draft of 'Analysis situs', Grothendieck is building an axiomatic theory of elementary 'figures'. The primitive data are three relations on a set M of figures: ≤ (part of / inclusion), ≪ (contained in the interior; a dotted variant written ∘≪ also appears) and |o| ('étrangers', i.e. disjoint interiors). These are constrained by axioms Mag 1–4. Further axioms Mog L1 (divisibility) and Mog L2 come on the next page. The test model is 'dimension 1'. On the previous page L was a totally ordered set. Section B now lets (L,≤) be an arbitrary poset. The figures are M = M_0 ⊔ M_1, with points P_x = {{x}} for x ∈ L and segments S_{a,b} = {[a,b],{a},{b}} for a<b. Their supports are |P_x| = {x} and |S_{a,b}| = [a,b], with naive interior |S_{a,b}|° = ]a,b[.

What the page does. Grothendieck defines |o| by explicit order-theoretic formulas and compares them with set-theoretic disjointness of interiors.
(1) P_x |o| P_y iff x<y or y<x, i.e. {x,y} is a comparable 2-element subset (perhaps 'Dcomp_2(L)'). This implies x≠y, i.e. |P_x|°∩|P_y|°=∅. The converse fails for incomparable distinct points.
(2) P_x |o| S_{a,b} iff x≤a or x≥b. This implies x ∉ ]a,b[. The converse fails, for example when x is incomparable to a or b but not strictly between them.
(3) S_{a,b} |o| S_{a',b'} iff a<b≤a'<b' or a'<b'≤a<b. This implies the open intervals are disjoint. Grothendieck marks the failure of the converse with a '?'. It does fail: with non-comparable endpoints, and even in a total order when L is not dense (]a,b[=∅).

The point is that the explicit formulas make it easy to check Mag 1 directly: ≤ and the derived relation are orders, and |o| is symmetric and antireflexive. A marginal NB notes a very special 'dimension 1' feature: two figures are either related in some way, equal, or strangers.

He then checks the remaining axioms.
- Mag 2 holds. One computes X ≪ Y iff (x=y for two points), (a≤x≤b for P_x and S_{a,b}), or (a'≤a<b≤b' for two segments). Hence X ≪ Y iff |X| ⊂ |Y| (closed supports), and on M_1 the relations ≪ and ∘≪ coincide.
- Mag 3 (strangeness is inherited by interior-subfigures) holds.
- Mag 4 (a 'no common part ⇒ strangers' type axiom; symbol unclear) holds.

Finally, minimal elements:
- The P_x are minimal both for ≤ and for ∘≪, and they are the only ≤-minimal figures.
- For ∘≪ there are also the 'pseudo-figures' S_{a,b} with ]a,b[ = ∅, i.e. b covers a.
- The 'liens' (junctions) between them are the P_x, so the set of liens is identified with L.

This prepares the next page, where divisibility (Mog L1) is shown to be equivalent to density of the poset, and Mog L2 to a separation condition on the order (intersections of ≤c over c>a).
errors: Second line: 'x ≤ a ou y ≥ b' should read 'x ≤ a ou x ≥ b' (slip of variable).
The P_x/P_x line is written with ⟺ |P_x|°∩|P_y|°=∅ in the top-right margin. It should be only ⇒ (equivalence holds only for total orders), as the line below in fact states.

For segments, the converse fails even in a total order when L is not divisible (]a,b[=∅ gives empty interiors that are disjoint from everything). So the '?' should be a definite 'no'; this is consistent with the next page's divisibility discussion.

Mag 4 as stated ('X ⊥ Y_0 ⇒ X|o|Y', symbol unclear) needs care for incomparable distinct points, which are not |o|. Whether it is 'OK' depends on the exact reading of the hypothesis, which cannot be confirmed from the image.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of 'figures' with three primitive relations: part-of (≤), interior containment (≪), strangeness/disjoint interiors (|o|), subject to axioms Mag 1–4.
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology: parthood, non-tangential proper part, discreteness/disconnection (as in RCC-8 / contact algebras / Whiteheadian point-free geometry).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992), Dimov–Vakarelov (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic mention of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); no axiomatics published.

ideas.what: 1-dimensional test model built from an arbitrary poset: points and closed 'segments' [a,b], with |o| defined by order formulas and compared to disjointness of open intervals.
ideas.modern_name: Interval/segment model of a poset; order-theoretic interval topology

ideas.what: Identification of ∘≪-minimal 'pseudo-figures' as covering pairs (empty open interval). The 'liens' are the points, so the set of junctions is identified with L.
ideas.modern_name: Covering relations / gaps in a poset; atoms vs. junction points

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck was in effect developing a point-free mereotopology (parthood, interior-parthood, disjointness, with a divisibility axiom = density) to found tame topology. He tested it on order-theoretic models. This parallels, apparently independently, the RCC/contact-algebra literature in AI and philosophy, which never cites this.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links Grothendieck's tame-topology program to mereotopology and point-free topology. Comparing his Mag/Mog axioms with RCC/contact-algebra representation theorems could clarify what he was aiming at.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is routine verification in a simple poset model. The interest is contextual: an unpublished mereotopological axiomatics by Grothendieck, not connected in the literature to point-free/region-based topology.
transcription_corrections: 'x ≤ a ou y ≥ b' is in the manuscript, but mathematically means x ≤ a or x ≥ b.
Top-right marginal reads '⟺ |P_x|°∩|P_y|° = ∅' attached to the first line (with the remark 'mais l'implication inverse pas valable en général' below the arrow).
NB in the left margin: 'X ≸ Y ⟺ X=Y ou X|o|Y' (comparison symbol uncertain), followed by 'chose très spéciale : dim 1 ...'.

'il y a en plus éléments minimaux pour ∘≪' is duplicated in the machine transcription; the manuscript says once: '...mais comme minimaux pour ∘≪, il y a en plus les S_{a,b} tels que |S_{a,b}|° = ]a,b[ = ∅'.
Last line: 'Entre eux, les liens sont les P_x, i.e. l'ensemble des liens s'identifie à L.'
